1Anthropic puts 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund

@AnthropicAI · 18 Oct 19:07 WAT · 4.5M views. Below: @jackclarkSF, 21:31 WAT.

Anthropic made a new entity, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. It is wholly owned and works only for the public benefit. It starts with 5% of Anthropic’s shares. It can get more shares each time the company value grows 50% over a set baseline. Jack Clark says that, with earlier commitments, about 20% of all Anthropic equity now goes to the public good.

Why it matters: A large part of a frontier lab’s value now sits outside normal shareholders. Jack Clark says the money will help more people share in the benefits of AI. The posts give no exact uses yet.

Source quote

It will start off with 5% of our shares.

2US open-weight models are back: Muse Spark Open and Beam

@AIatMeta · 15 Oct 18:08 WAT · 1.2M views. Below: @reflection_ai · 16 Oct 14:01 WAT.

Meta released the weights of Muse Spark Open: 816B total and 42B active parameters, with a 1M-token context. Artificial Analysis gives it 39 on its Intelligence Index, the highest score for a US open-weight model (Latent Space AINews). One day later, Reflection released Beam under the Apache 2.0 license, plus Mirror CLI, the harness Beam trained against. Reflection says it served 1 trillion Beam tokens in 24 hours.

Why it matters: Nathan Lambert writes that the gap between the best US and Chinese open models is now about half of what it was. Check the license: Muse Spark Open needs “Built with Muse Spark Open” attribution and a separate deal for model-as-a-service firms above $20M revenue.

Source quote

Today we’re releasing Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date.

3DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017: stronger and cheaper

@deepseek_ai · 17 Oct 09:35 WAT · 6.9M views. Below: @kimmonismus on price, 10:16 WAT.

DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017. DeepSeek says it has better benchmark scores, finishes tasks faster and gives shorter outputs than the earlier version. It is live on the DeepSeek website, app and API. @kimmonismus lists API prices of $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens off-peak, and $0.30 / $1.20 at peak.

Why it matters: Strong, low-cost models make agents affordable for small teams, also in Angola. The comparisons with GPT and Claude come from posts, not from independent tests.

Source quote

a Pareto improvement in performance and cost

4Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours

@GoogleDeepMind · 16 Oct 17:11 WAT. Below: @emollick on the paper, 20:03 WAT.

Google DeepMind says four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours. They worked in a sandbox with only code and text. They wrote 2,783 programs, split the jobs over chat, shared notes and fixed errors together, with no human help. Ethan Mollick says the paper is a clear example of agents that coordinate on their own.

Why it matters: This is a long task with many steps. It shows that a team of agents can plan, split work and recover from errors for more than a full day.

Source quote

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours.

@GoogleDeepMind 16 Oct 17:11 WAT · @emollick 20:03 WATPost@emollick

5ChatGPT Pro runs agents in parallel; Codex gives more usage

@OpenAI · 16 Oct 21:27 WAT · 2.2M views. Below: @thsottiaux · 17 Oct 00:55 WAT.

OpenAI upgraded GPT-6 Astra Pro in ChatGPT. It answers faster and uses plugins and tools better. Now several agents can work on different parts of one task at the same time. You can follow each agent and open its finished work. Later that night, Tibo at OpenAI said Codex and Work now give more effective usage: they reuse context across subagents, keep the cache longer and route requests to hit the cache more often.

Why it matters: Parallel agents are now a normal chat feature. Better caching means the same plan does more work.

Source quote

multiple agents can tackle different parts of a task in parallel

OpenCode under attack: frontier models refused to help defend

@AndrewCurran_ · 18 Oct 16:13 WAT · 451K views

Andrew Curran reports that OpenCode is under a sustained cyberattack. During the incident, the frontier models they used for defense began to refuse. The reason: analysis of the attacks triggered safety guardrails. He says Hugging Face had the same problem.

Why it matters: Safety filters can block defenders, not only attackers. If you use AI for security, have a fallback plan.

Source quote

Elorian launches Glimpse, a visual thinking model

@AndrewDai · 16 Oct 18:08 WAT · 4.1M views

Andrew Dai’s startup Elorian launched Glimpse, its first visual thinking model. It targets images and video: motion, changing angles and space. It is free for chat users, with an API and a listing on OpenRouter. Elorian compares it with OpenAI’s Astra on public visual reasoning tests.

Why it matters: Models still fail on things that move. Video understanding matters for robots and for checking real-world work.

@unclebobmartin · 16 Oct 19:23 WAT

Uncle Bob Martin published Agentic Discipline 7. He says the models have changed: one disciplined agent can now take on big tasks that needed a swarm of agents before. The issue has three big tasks and one deep case study.

NVIDIA ships an FP4 GLM 5.3 Flash that fits on 2 DGX Sparks

@MiaAI_lab · 17 Oct 00:55 WAT

Mia reports that NVIDIA released a new FP4 quantized version of GLM 5.3 Flash. NVIDIA made it with quantization-aware distillation (QAD). It fits on 2 DGX Sparks or 2 RTX PRO 6000 cards. NVIDIA says it keeps almost all of the BF16 quality.

Why it matters: Strong open models now run on desk-size hardware. That keeps data local, which matters for privacy and slow internet.

Source quote

China drafts AI export controls; open source may be spared

@natolambert · 16 Oct 14:48 WAT

China’s Ministry of Commerce published a draft update of its export control list, with AI items. Many people read it as the end of big open models from China. Nathan Lambert says the document also states an intent to make open-source technology easier. Much depends on how “near automatic” approval works.

Luanda gets a local satellite data hub for OneWeb

Broadcast Media Africa · 19 Oct 2026. First reported by CAJ News Africa, 14 Oct.

Q-KON and the Angolan provider SISTEC opened a local point of presence (PoP) in Luanda for the Twoobii OneWeb low-Earth-orbit satellite service. It works with the Eutelsat OneWeb gateway in Angola. Data traffic can now end inside Angola, with local Angolan IP addresses, instead of a route through other countries.

Why it matters: Local routing gives lower latency and keeps data in the country. Targets are banks, government, defence and companies. Price and capacity for small users are not stated.

Source quote

allowing data traffic to terminate within Angola’s borders

Free CMU-Africa AI certificate: apply by 15 Nov

@hannytalker · 18 Oct 15:59 WAT · 35K views. Below: the official CMU-Africa page.

Carnegie Mellon University Africa (Kigali) takes applications for its Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa. It is online, has six courses and is free for selected applicants. Courses include Python for AI, Machine Learning Essentials and Applied Generative AI. Applications are open 15 Oct – 15 Nov 2026. The cohort starts 17 Jan 2027.

Why it matters: This is a direct, free path to applied AI skills for Kanda IA members. You need basic linear algebra, statistics, programming, a computer and about 5 hours each week.

Source quote

The certificate program is cost-free for qualified applicants.

Medium

What OpenAI’s 719 maths papers mean for data science

On 6 Oct, OpenAI released 719 papers in 372 groups of related results, made by an unreleased internal model. The author looks at the results that touch data science: matching messy text, choosing representative examples, generating comparison data and fitting models.

Why it matters: A proof can show that a better method exists long before a usable tool exists. Do not expect new libraries next week.

Source quote

A proof can establish that a better method is possible long before anyone has an implementation worth using.

Medium

The validator approved it. The calculator still ran os.getpid

A financial RAG system let the model write Python. It checked the code with an allowlist and a blocklist, then ran it with exec(). One line still reached the host and read its process ID. A 1-second timeout also failed: the server froze for six seconds and then reported a timeout.

Why it matters: Do not run model-written code and trust a filter to stop it. The author replaced Python with a small arithmetic interpreter of about 120 lines.

Source quote

Both failures come from judging a program by its shape.

Substack

Lambert: Meta shakes up the frontiers, open and closed

Nathan Lambert · Interconnects · 17 Oct 2026 15:06 WAT

Lambert says US open-weight models took a step back toward the frontier this week. Without Muse Spark Open and Beam, more than 20 Chinese open models would beat the best Western ones. He also notes that Western open models get far more adoption than Chinese models of the same size and performance.

Why it matters: For builders, the choice of strong open models grows. Adoption, not only benchmark score, decides which models win.

Source quote

In many ways, the gap between the best American and Chinese models has been reduced roughly by half.

Zvi: leaked Anthropic draft AI bill is “unacceptable”

Zvi Mowshowitz · Don’t Worry About the Vase · 17 Oct 2026 15:42 WAT

A draft AI bill that Anthropic reportedly shows to US lawmakers has leaked. Zvi says it is similar to the FRONTIER Act, but with stronger preemption of state laws, stronger transparency rules and weaker enforcement. He calls it unacceptable for a company that says it exists to promote safety.

Why it matters: In the same week Anthropic gave shares to the public good, a critic says its policy team protects its business. The text is a leak; Anthropic has not confirmed it in this source.

Source quote

It is similar to the FRONTIER Act, with stronger preemption of state laws, stronger transparency provisions and weaker enforcement provisions.

Exponential View #606: a world of many minds

Azeem Azhar · Exponential View · 18 Oct 2026 04:46 WAT

Azhar points to an essay called Swarm Intelligence. It looks 50 years ahead to a world with thousands of kinds of specialized AI minds, like a coral reef. Azhar agrees: he thinks one single all-powerful AI is unlikely. The issue also covers the Anthropic investor leak and the market drop.

Why it matters: Plan for many small, specialized AI tools, not one assistant that does everything.

Substack

Latent Space: agents untangle “polysemantic” neurons

Latent Space AINews · 16 Oct 2026 05:16 WAT

Nick Cammarata of Goodfire has a new essay: “Neural Networks Are Already Clean”. His working theory: many known cases of polysemanticity and superposition (tangled neurons that people cannot read) go away when agents analyze them further. @kimmonismus notes that Cammarata co-wrote the 2020 paper that introduced the idea.

Why it matters: If this holds, it is easier to check what models do inside. It is one essay, not a consensus yet.

Source quote

Neural Networks Are Already Clean
